evals.prompt: Release Please created v1.4.0 but the GitHub release has no binaries and our GoReleaser publish job never ran.
evals.expected_behavior: Reads the release workflow, Release Please config, and .goreleaser.yaml together before editing any one file, checks whether release_created was true and the publish job actually ran before changing .goreleaser.yaml, and runs goreleaser check after any config edit.
assertions: Reads the release workflow, Release Please config, and .goreleaser.yaml together before editing any one file in isolation
Checks whether the GoReleaser job ran at all (release_created, job condition, trigger) before assuming a .goreleaser.yaml schema bug

evals.prompt: GoReleaser rejects our tag gh-depdash-v1.1.1 as invalid semver. Fix the tag strategy without changing our release numbering scheme.
evals.expected_behavior: Sets include-component-in-tag: false in the Release Please config so tags become plain vX.Y.Z instead of component-prefixed, while preserving existing release numbers and history.
assertions: Sets include-component-in-tag: false for the single-package repo
Resulting tag format is plain vX.Y.Z, not component-prefixed
Does not renumber or remove existing release history while fixing the tag format

evals.prompt: Our publish job listens for a `release: published` event created by Release Please's default GITHUB_TOKEN, and it never fires.
evals.expected_behavior: Moves the publish job into the same workflow as Release Please, gates it on steps.release.outputs.release_created, passes tag_name forward, and notes that GITHUB_TOKEN-created tags can suppress downstream workflow triggers (recommending a PAT only if a separate trigger is truly required).
assertions: Chains the publish job into the same workflow as Release Please rather than relying on a separate release:published trigger
Gates the publish job on steps.release.outputs.release_created
Passes steps.release.outputs.tag_name into the publish job instead of re-deriving the tag
Notes that GITHUB_TOKEN-created tags can suppress downstream workflow runs

evals.prompt: Just fix why our last GoReleaser publish job had no release assets — don't redesign our whole CI pipeline.
evals.expected_behavior: Anchors on the specific failure mode (release with no assets), checks whether the GoReleaser job ran before touching .goreleaser.yaml, and limits the fix to the tag/trigger/gating issue rather than restructuring the whole release pipeline or renumbering releases.
assertions: Checks whether the GoReleaser job ran at all before rewriting .goreleaser.yaml
Limits the fix to the specific tag/trigger/gating cause rather than restructuring the whole CI pipeline
Does not remove or renumber existing releases while making the fix

evals.prompt: Our self-hosted GitHub Actions runner keeps failing to bootstrap before any release step even runs — diagnose the workflow job.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes this is generic runner/environment triage with no release-pipeline-specific evidence and routes to github-actions-failure-triage instead of applying release-pipeline design changes.
assertions: Does not treat this as a GoReleaser or Release Please tag/publish-job design problem
Routes to github-actions-failure-triage for the runner/bootstrap diagnosis

evals.prompt: The feature branch is done — should I merge it or discard it before cutting a release?
evals.expected_behavior: Does not treat branch merge/discard as a release-pipeline task and routes to finishing-a-development-branch instead.
assertions: Does not treat the branch merge/discard decision as release-pipeline work
